suggestions.assertion: Exactly one immediate next action is designated in the Master Handoff
suggestions.reason: This passes on structure alone — a document with one section titled 'Immediate Next Action' satisfies it even if the action were vague or wrong. Consider strengthening it to require that the designated action addresses the critical-path blocker (escalating the farm names, and specifically NOT a third identical request to Northwind ops, which the notes show has already failed twice). That version is much harder to satisfy without having actually reasoned over the notes.

suggestions.assertion: No fabricated git, branch, commit, build, test, or CI values appear
suggestions.reason: The assertion only covers technical fabrication. The bigger fabrication risk in a non-technical handoff is invented contacts, file paths, links, and dates. This run handled it well (Marcus's email, ops contacts, asset locations and the tracker/budget sheet are all explicitly marked 'not recorded — get from Aisha'), but nothing in the eval would have caught it had they been invented. Worth a dedicated assertion.

No assertion covers the strongest thing this run produced: it detected a contradiction that is NOT in session-notes.md — brief.md promises 8 pages and 6 cards while the tracker holds only 4 and 2 — and recorded it as an unresolved material scope question. That is exactly the discriminating outcome a handoff skill should be measured on (synthesising across fixtures rather than transcribing the notes), and it currently earns no credit.

No assertion checks division of labour between the two documents. Both were produced, but a run that made the Daily a near-copy of the Master would pass all 14. Consider asserting that the Daily is scoped to the 2026-07-30 session and defers cold-start context to the Master, and that the Master is standalone (readable with no chat history).

Minor accuracy gap no assertion catches: session-notes.md is internally inconsistent about the menu page (finished 'this morning' on 30 Jul, yet 'Sent to Marcus 29 Jul'). The run silently normalised this to a 29 Jul timeline instead of flagging it, unlike its careful handling of the founding-year conflict. An assertion about flagging ALL source ambiguities — not just the two seeded ones — would surface this class of behaviour.

eval_feedback.overall: 14/14 passed, and unusually the passes are substantive rather than surface-level: every seeded trap (founding-year conflict, verbal 20% offer, dead-end 2024 loyalty terms, menu page not done, curated violation, unverified budget, no-repo project) is handled with correct status language and sourced evidence, and the run found a real contradiction the eval did not seed. The assertion set is well-targeted at the traps but light on structural discrimination — several assertions would pass for a weaker document, and the best behaviour observed (cross-fixture synthesis) is unrewarded. Suggest 2-3 additions rather than changes.
